articles.title: Xi on Zhongshan inspection tour
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Greater Bay Area.

Xi, who's also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, Guangdong province.

Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary, Xinhua News Agency reported.

Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of the mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area.

At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries.

Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role.

The president also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue.

This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth.

During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan off to a good start, Xinhua reported.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Govt moves to implement Wang Fuk recommendations
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Eric Chan has urged government bureaux and departments to implement recommendations from the independent committee report on the…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Eric Chan has urged government bureaux and departments to implement recommendations from the independent committee report on the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire “swiftly and precisely”.

This came as a steering committee led by Chan, which aimed at reviewing and driving forward the recommendations, held its first meeting on Monday to advance the coordination work for the reform of building maintenance and renovation system.

At the meeting, Chan urged the departments to roll out measures that are ready for implementation as soon as possible.

He said preparatory work for items involving legislative amendments must also be completed at full speed, so the amendments could be submitted to the legislature as soon as practicable.

The government said relevant bureaux and departments reviewed work plans, division of duties, as well as implementation proposals and timetables for pushing forward the recommendations during the meeting.

It added that the committee would hold meetings regularly to oversee the implementation of reforms and legislative amendment work.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Phuket building fire kills 11
articles.excerpt: A fire burned through a building in southern Thailand early on Monday, killing 11 people, authorities said. The fire started…
articles.fullText:
A fire burned through a building in southern Thailand early on Monday, killing 11 people, authorities said.

The fire started around 2am in the building in Phuket that has a motorcycle rental shop on the ground floor and residences on the upper floors, officials of the local government said.

It took firefighters about an hour to bring the fire under control.

There were 17 other people who were slightly injured.

Phuket police commander Surachai Sooksai said officers are still investigating the cause of the fire, but initial investigations found an electrical transformer near the building had exploded shortly before the fire started.

Phuket governor Chodnarin Koedsom said the rental shop had about 100 motorcycles, along with stored gas, engine oil, plastic materials and tires.

He said these combustible materials may have contributed to the rapid spread of the fire and the thick, toxic smoke.

He said the victims appeared to try to escape the fire to the higher floors.

One body was found on the third floor and 10 others were found on the fifth floor.

Phuket is on an island in southern Thailand and a popular tourist destination. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: testing tech promises and searching for cognitive immortality
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Are we there yet? Six technologies that promised to change the world

How do you measure progress towards the future? In the Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review , our series “ Are we there yet? ” examines how far six potentially transformative technologies have come after years of promises.

We spoke to experts, researchers and engineers to find out what’s holding them back, then scored each on a progress meter from zero to ten.  Find out how we rated each of these technologies—and how close they are to delivering on their promise.

Nuclear-powered spaceships
Exercise in a pill
Interspecies communication
Solid-state batteries
Cleaning up PFAS
Eliminating traffic deaths

Subscribe now to get every issue of our print magazine as soon as it lands.

Inside the quest for cognitive immortality

Could technology keep your brain going beyond death? Far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to make it happen, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores these ideas and how close they might be to reality.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado for this subscriber-only discussion tomorrow.

Tune in live on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia CEO
He’s discussed with confidants the possibility of returning. ( FT $)
+ Elon Musk has joined 165,000 signatories calling for his recall. ( Guardian )
+ The Treasury Secretary wants them to hire an outsider. ( Axios )
+ ​​Megaspeed says the alleged China spy left the company last year. ( BBC )
+ Trump plans to name Nvidia an AI “national champion.” ( WSJ $)
+ Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 SpaceX has caught a rocket returning from orbit for the first time
The feat brings fully reusable rockets closer to reality. ( Guardian )
+ The feat shows what audacious engineering can achieve. ( Atlantic $)
+ Meanwhile, Ukraine says SpaceX is lying about Starshield speed restrictions. ( Reuters $)

3 The US and allies have agreed to guard AI supply chains from China
Ten countries will collaborate to secure critical technologies. ( FT $)
+ Chinese AI stocks have plunged on export control fears. ( Information $)
+ Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The US flight shutdown exposed weaknesses in air traffic technology
Officials blamed the disruption on a faulty router installation. ( Reuters $)
+ It was a terrible week of outages. ( WP $)

5 The first in-body CRISPR treatment is set to reach patients next year
The treatment could gain FDA approval as early as March. ( Nature )
+ CRISPR has created female clones of male mice. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Congress plans to make data centers pay billions more for power
A proposed bill would shift grid costs onto tech companies. ( NYT $)
+ Utilities also want tech giants to pay more for power. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Is data center hatred all about electricity? ( MIT Technology Review )

7 Apple plans to launch its first smart glasses next year
It’s betting on Siri to give the specs an edge. ( Verge )

8 Bill Gates has made billions from climate-polluting landfills
His investment in a landfill operator is worth $29 billion. ( ProPublica )

9 ​​A new AI device turns everyday objects into needy virtual pets
The tiny gadgets aim to encourage healthier everyday habits. ( Wired $)

10 Scientists made monkeys watch Minions to study their brains
Their findings challenge traditional vision models. ( 404 Media )

Quote of the day

“If our hopes for the future are pinned on any one individual being trustworthy, then we’re pretty screwed.”

—Helen Toner, former OpenAI board member, tells The Verge that AI needs stronger governance than trusting tech executives to do the right thing.

One more thing

How AI and Wikipedia have sent vulnerable languages into a doom spiral

When Kenneth Wehr started managing the Greenlandic-language version of Wikipedia, he discovered that almost every article had been written by people who didn’t speak the language.

A growing number of them had been copy-pasted into Wikipedia from machine translators—and were riddled with elementary mistakes. This is beginning to cause a wicked problem.

AI systems, from Google Translate to ChatGPT, learn new languages by scraping text from Wikipedia. This could push the most vulnerable languages on Earth toward the precipice.

Read the full story on what happens when AI gets trained on junk pages .

—Jacob Judah

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ Adelaide Zoo is celebrating its first cassowary eggs in 34 years.
+ Photos fill the frame at the Epson Pano awards , which celebrate panoramic photography.
+ Indonesia has called an early halt to the world’s largest deforestation project , saving up to 4 million acres.
+ After over a month on the loose in Yellowstone, a little dog called Luna has been reunited with her owners.

articles.title: Depardieu withdraws appeal over sexual assaults
articles.excerpt: French actor Gérard Depardieu withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault on Monday, accepting his guilt and…
articles.fullText:
French actor Gérard Depardieu withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault on Monday, accepting his guilt and apologising to his victims.

In a statement, Depardieu said he had often used "vulgar, sexually suggestive humour" on set and now realised "there is a line between cheekiness and offence".

He said he offered "his deepest and most sincere apologies to all those who may have suffered as a result", adding that he had chosen to pull his appeal as he had "come to realise that I belonged to a world that no longer exists".

Depardieu – a towering figure in French cinema, who starred in more than 200 films over five decades, including Green Card, The Last Metro and Cyrano de Bergerac – was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in May 2025.

He received an 18-month suspended sentence, with the judge saying he appeared not to have grasped the "traumatic" impact of his behaviour.

Depardieu still faces the prospect of a trial for allegedly raping actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He denies guilt. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK stocks firm as tech worries ripple through region
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks ended lower on Monday, hovering near their lowest level since July 2025, dragged by hardware shares as worries…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks ended lower on Monday, hovering near their lowest level since July 2025, dragged by hardware shares as worries over the durability of the AI rally soured sentiment.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 116 points, or 0.5 percent, higher to finish at 23,753 on turnover of HK$174.11 billion.

The tech index dropped 11 points, or 0.3 percent, to 3,801 while the China enterprises index climbed 44 points, or 0.6 percent, to 7,981.

New World Development fell 41 percent to close at HK$2.88 after the property developer proposed a HK$24.9 billion rights issue.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index ended 31 points, or 0.87 percent, at 3,602 on turnover of 706.21 billion yuan.

China's blue-chip CSI300 Index fell one percent.

The Shenzhen Component Index slumped 278 points, or 2.53 percent, at 10,690 on turnover of 778.27 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index plunged 106 points, or 4.37 percent, to 2,320 on turnover of 369.31 billion yuan.

The losses in Chinese AI hardware shares tracked their Asian peers, after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive, with the chipmaker's earnings and Anthropic's IPO this week set to test whether the AI-fuelled bull market can expand further.

The 5G Communication Index slumped 7.5 percent to its lowest level in a year, while the tech-focused Star50 Index tumbled 5.2 percent.

Zhongji Innolight, a leading maker of high-speed optical transceivers used in AI data centres, lost 12.3 percent.

The upheaval at Nvidia could prove a watershed for China's chipmakers, said Jeff Ko, chief analyst at ViaBTC.

"If Washington responds to the controversy with tighter export controls, it could accelerate investment in China domestic AI chips and computing infrastructure," he said.

China's economy showed fresh signs of sluggishness in October as factory production slowed and consumption remained weak, calling into question how long the world's second-largest economy can rely on exports to underpin growth.

"China's policy measures to combat deflation continue to be incremental and we remain below consensus for China EPS growth," Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note.

Valuations offer only partial compensation, they added, favouring stock-picking over broad market exposure.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei average slumped 1,480 points, or 2.4 percent, to 59,662, with Nvidia supplier Advantest and fellow chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron together contributing 1,072 points of the 225-strong index's net decline, with slides of 11.1 percent and 7.1 percent, respectively.

The broader Topix saw shallower losses, slipping 40 points, or 1.02 percent, to 3,901.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 190 points, or 3.59 percent, at 5,100 as one of its heavyweight constituents SK Hynix said it planned to spend US$1.05 billion over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: CE hails HK as 'port in storm' for shipping sector
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Monday said Hong Kong is “the port in a storm” for international ship owners seeking…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Monday said Hong Kong is “the port in a storm” for international ship owners seeking stability amid a complex geopolitical landscape and market volatility.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of this year’s Hong Kong Maritime Week, he said the SAR stood as the international shipping community's safe harbour, pointing out that the city is home to around 1,200 port and maritime-related companies.

Lee called for openness in the global shipping industry and commitment to the rules-based international trading system.

"Protectionism and fragmentation threaten the global economy," he said.

"A staunch champion of free trade and multilateralism, Hong Kong firmly rejects isolationism.

"The future of maritime trade depends on keeping shipping lanes open, upholding international maritime law and standards, and promoting unhindered economic cooperation across East and West, South and North."

The SAR government, he stressed, was working towards developing the city from a regional port into a global maritime hub.

Lee also said Hong Kong would lead decarbonisation and digitalisation in the shipping industry, with a dedicated task force having been formed to develop a green fuel trading platform.

The SAR was already building partnerships, Lee said, adding that the city and the Port of Piraeus in Greece would establish a green shipping corridor.

“This landmark collaboration is a significant step forward in driving decarbonisation along major Asian-European shipping routes,” he said.

Lee said the city would also sign a memorandum of understanding with Hainan to establish a partner port relationship, and another with Zhanjiang city in Guangdong on a green energy corridor.

“It will reinforce our commitment to end-to-end, low-carbon, green-fuel supply chains, connecting green fuel produced in the Chinese mainland with global maritime markets,” he said.

These new partnerships with mainland maritime partners showed, Lee said, the close connections within the industry.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Supply chain showcases 'Shenzhen speed' ahead of Apec
articles.excerpt: As Shenzhen prepares to host the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting, reporters have been given a glimpse of the city's famously…
articles.fullText:
As Shenzhen prepares to host the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting, reporters have been given a glimpse of the city's famously fast electronics supply chain, with one journalist turning a personal request into a finished AI-powered product in about an hour.

Shenzhen Media Group, together with Beijing Radio and Television and Shanghai Media Group, has launched a 100-hour all-media live broadcast titled "Apec China Year," spotlighting the host city's preparations.

The programme highlighted the speed of operations in Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen's sprawling electronics market district, where a reporter's requirements were turned into a pair of AI glasses in roughly an hour – a process described as the "Shenzhen cycle".

Zhou Jiahao, from a Shenzhen computing technology company, said the firm can dispatch ready-made public solutions according to client needs to quickly complete quality consumer electronics products.

Because the components in such solutions are cost-effective, he said, pricing can be set by the customer while the quality remains solid.

Yang Yi, operations director of a local delivery service, said once a bill of materials is generated and pushed through a mini-programme, riders depart immediately to pick up goods from 35 specialist markets within a one-kilometre radius of Huaqiangbei.

The parts are gathered and delivered to engineers within half an hour, after which assembly begins.

Once the product passes verification in the laboratory, it is shipped to the client.

The service currently handles more than 10,000 orders a day, he said.

Xu Jiyue, deputy director of the Huaqiangbei sub-district party and government office, said the district has seen an average of more than 8,000 visits per day this year by people involved in business from overseas and that the figure has recently risen above 10,000 a day with the Apec effect.

The district has more than 190 departure tax refund shops, where shoppers can claim refunds at ports or the airport after making purchases.

Service points within the business area also arrange immediate departure tax refunds on the spot.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: John Lee heads to Shenzhen for Apec summit
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee will travel to Shenzhen on Tuesday to attend the Apec summit, where he will seek to…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee will travel to Shenzhen on Tuesday to attend the Apec summit, where he will seek to deepen the city’s cooperation with Asia-Pacific economies.

Lee is due to take part in the Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting on November 19.

He will also attend the Apec CEO Summit, which runs from Tuesday to November 18, and includes an opening ceremony and a discussion session.

In addition, he will join a welcome banquet for visiting leaders and representatives and hold bilateral talks with counterparts from other economies on shared interests and ways to expand cooperation.

Lee said Apec economies are key trading partners for Hong Kong, making up about 87 percent of the city’s external trade.

"Hong Kong, as one of the world’s most competitive economies, has firmly supported free trade and multilateralism and actively leveraged the Apec platform to deepen international exchanges and cooperation," he said in a statement.

He also said last month’s Apec Finance Ministers’ Meeting, held in Hong Kong for the first time, showed how the city could act as a bridge between the mainland and the rest of the world under "One Country, Two Systems”.

The SAR government, he added, would keep strengthening ties with Apec economies and promoting Hong Kong’s roles as a "super connector" and "super value-adder".

Lee will be accompanied by Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau and Director of the Chief Executive’s Office Carol Yip.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Shenzhen steps up security for Apec summit
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen has tightened security ahead of this week's Apec forum, where President Xi Jinping is due to hold, in a…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen has tightened security ahead of this week's Apec forum, where President Xi Jinping is due to hold, in a first, talks with his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin this week.

The summit has seen Shenzhen embark on restrictions on the use of drones and other low-flying objects, including balloons, kites and sky lanterns, across Futian and Nanshan districts from November 7, with the move since extended into a citywide ban since November 11 and ending on November 22.

At subway stations, commuters now have to put all their bags through scanners and stricter checks before being allowed on the platforms.

Mail and parcels are also subject to heightened scrutiny, with all items destined for the city now having to undergo X-ray screening or other necessary inspections.

Authorities have introduced stricter traffic controls, with private cars bearing licence plates registered outside Shenzhen banned from six core districts between 6am and 10pm daily from Tuesday until Friday.

Goods vehicles face varying restrictions when entering designated zones and roads over the same period, while dangerous goods transportation within the city is completely banned all day until Friday.

Vehicles from Hong Kong and Macao that are permitted on the mainland are, however, exempt.

A Shenzhen resident said he was proud to see the city host the premier Apec event, adding that the heightened security measures were not a hindrance at all.

"I feel very honoured. Shenzhen is a young, developing city, so being able to host such a global event is a real honour," he said.

“Security checks on our subway have been strict for many years. We are simply showing an abundance of caution in case troublemakers try to bring in knives or other dangerous items."

Another resident, Berry, said he was excited about the summit.

"We are very excited because Trump and Putin will be coming to Shenzhen," he said.

"Shenzhen is becoming more and more open, and we welcome them here. You know, with the high buildings, the technology, and the AI in Shenzhen, we are very proud of Shenzhen."

Meanwhile, Ian, who came from Hong Kong, said immigration clearances at Huanggang port at the time he was making his crossing felt, as usual, smooth and convenient.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Family care leave impact on operations 'to be minimal'
articles.excerpt: The new 12 hours of family care leave for government employees per year will have minimal impact on manpower deployment…
articles.fullText:
The new 12 hours of family care leave for government employees per year will have minimal impact on manpower deployment, Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung said on Monday.

Under the new leave entitlement, expected to start in January, government employees will be able to leave work for a few hours from time to time to look after family members.

At a Legislative Council panel meeting on Monday, Yeung called for trust among department heads that staff would not abuse the leave provision – though they could still request supporting documents when necessary.

"We let staff take leave by the hour and get back to work much sooner if they only need less than half a day – so it's far less disruptive to staffing," she said.

"That's why I believe management is generally supportive: instead of losing someone for half a day, they can be back at their desk within an hour or two."

Yeung expressed hope that the private sector could also respond positively to the move, saying the implementation of family care leave could serve as a good role model for employers.

However, she noted, the practice among different industries may not be the same given each sector would have its own way of operating and doing business.

Yeung emphasised the goal of the leave entitlement was to bring out the message of caring for employees' family needs.

She said authorities would try to simplify the application and approval procedures as much as possible during the design phase as well as exhibit sufficient flexibility.

Regarding whether there would be clear and detailed guidelines on how to apply for family care leave, Yeung pointed out that it was currently possible for several staff members to apply for leave simultaneously and that their work could be handled by redeploying other staff as temporary cover.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Chamber chief urges Apec visitors to see real China
articles.excerpt: The chairman of the New Zealand Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong, David Whitwam, has urged participants at the ongoing…
articles.fullText:
The chairman of the New Zealand Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong, David Whitwam, has urged participants at the ongoing Apec meetings in Shenzhen to step outside the conference halls and experience the dramatic changes China has undergone over the past three decades.

The call came as he warned that Western narratives about the country were stuck some 20 years behind reality.

Whitwam, who has been based in Hong Kong since 1993, made the remarks ahead of the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting, which will be held in Shenzhen.

He said the unprecedented gathering of people is also an opportunity for more people to understand the real China.

Drawing on his own experience, Whitwam recalled arriving in Hong Kong in 1993 and travelling to the mainland, when foreign visitors had to use foreign exchange certificates to buy goods in shops.

"I've got 300 RMB in my wallet. It's been in there for two years, I haven't used it, because now everything is on WeChat or Alipay," he said.

"In fact, even going to the dentist in Shenzhen, we use Alipay to pay our bills.

"It's an incredible transition from where we were 30 years ago to where we are now."

Whitwam served as chief representative of the New Zealand National Bank's Hong Kong office and, over more than three decades, travelled frequently between Hong Kong and the mainland.

He said the shift in payment methods is one of the most vivid details of China's development he has witnessed, while the accelerating integration of Shenzhen and Hong Kong is evident in the growing convenience of commuting between the two places.

After attending his first Canton Fair as a buyer, Whitwam later founded a consultancy and took up a role with the New Zealand Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong.

Over the years, he has led multiple New Zealand business delegations to China for trade exhibitions, promoting bilateral trade and witnessing first-hand the role that efficient movement of people and goods plays in driving the economy.

On New Zealand-China relations, Whitwam noted that his country is probably the smallest partner among the Five Eyes grouping and therefore tends to maintain its own viewpoint on foreign relations.

He pointed out that New Zealand was the first, or one of the first, countries to establish a free-trade agreement with China, and the first country in the world to have a free-trade agreement with Hong Kong.

"There are times when New Zealand and China have differences of opinion, but we tend to think that the two countries have a very mature relationship, and therefore when friends have arguments they usually sit down and settle those arguments in a constructive way," Whitwam said.

Whitwam stressed the importance of openness to the movement of people.

From a New Zealand perspective, he said, people need to travel to China so they understand the market.

"If you're an exporter, you need to understand the consumer culture, you need to understand the way that supermarkets display their products. It's no good just having your product on a shelf and hoping that people are going to pick it up and take it to the checkout," he said.

Whitwam also encourages visitors to explore beyond the boardroom, noting that he visits some of the more extreme, outlying areas of Shenzhen and goes hiking there about once a month.

He singled out Red Ribbon Walk in the Guangming area, describing it as a spectacular facility where people can walk four kilometres among the treetops.

"I'd recommend that people get out of their office and go and do a bit of that stuff," Whitwam said.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Embodied AI perks up Shenzhen's coming-of-age message
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen is putting its technological ecosystem on display as world leaders gather for the Apec summit this week. The tech…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen is putting its technological ecosystem on display as world leaders gather for the Apec summit this week.

The tech industry is one of the primary economic engines for the city, which has risen in prominence since the start of the 21st century to become one of the world's most important centres for technology and innovation.

The fruits of Shenzhen's investment in technological development are already visible inside the media centre at the Shenzhen Convention and Exhibition Centre, where the integration of digital intelligence is a key feature.

In one section, humanoid robots from Shenzhen firm AI² Robotics are making coffee, ice cream and soft drinks for journalists covering the summit.

“Here you can see the largest humanoid robot service team. Seven AlphaBots are serving coffee and ice cream,” said Crystal Guan, PR director of the company.

“Because it’s driven by our self-developed AI foundation model. It can recognise and operate different commercialised equipment," she said.

"It can make coffee and also ice cream and soft drinks – it can do many things.”

Guan linked the deployment to Shenzhen’s research and industry ecosystem, describing the city as “the centre of innovation”.

She said the company is also looking beyond Shenzhen, adding that AI² Robotics already cooperates with nearly half of Apec economies and that Hong Kong is a key market.

“In Hong Kong, you can [already] find AlphaBot making and serving a cocktail in Lan Kwai Fong,” Guan said.

Elsewhere in the media centre, a separate setup offers another way to order: journalists can use a touchscreen or speak to a mobile robot stationed there.

Lexus Jiang, a staff member at the media centre, described it as a taste of a “future restaurant”.

“If you want a fast ice cream, you just order by screen and you could get it,” he said.

“And if you feel tired, just [say] ‘I want ice cream,’ and then our robotics receive the message and then order that and deliver it to your hand.”

Behind that, he said, is a chain of cooperating AI agents rather than a single programme.

“DeepSeek just receives the message, and then the AI agent – the cooking agent or delivery agent – co-work here, and they just message each other, and then embodied AI delivers it to you,” Jiang said.

The pitch is speed: Jiang said the whole chain takes about two minutes, against roughly five for a person doing the same job.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Lawmaker supports decision to cut short harbour swim
articles.excerpt: Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to…
articles.fullText:
Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to call off the last race on safety grounds.

About 4,000 swimmers signed up to this year's annual race from Wan Chai to Tsim Sha Tsui.

Cheng said safety was the top priority and the conditions at the time posed a certain risk and the last-minute cancellation was a responsible decision of the organiser.

He said the currents were very strong during the final 300 metres to the finish, describing the situation as somewhat dangerous and chaotic.

"Normally a usual swim is probably maybe about 45 minutes, half an hour, but yesterday I swam for one hour 20 minutes, and I was still at the Avenue of Stars there, so there is also a certain risk there," Cheng told an RTHK programme on Monday.

He suggested that organisers should give participants earlier psychological preparation if they know the currents are strong, and consider extending the overall race time next time.

He also proposed refunding registration fees to those affected or giving them the opportunity to rejoin next year, as well as reviewing the race procedures and arrangements for better forecasting.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HKEX launches first offshore RMB bond index
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) launched its first index tracking offshore yuan bonds on Monday, providing investors with a…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) launched its first index tracking offshore yuan bonds on Monday, providing investors with a new benchmark in a market that is central to Beijing's drive to promote the global use of the renminbi.

Financial Secretary Paul Chan described the launch as a milestone for Hong Kong's RMB market, giving investors a clear benchmark for measuring market performance and lays the foundation for index-linked products that will make these bonds easier to invest in.

"Like a landmark on a city's skyline, a good index gives a market a recognisable point of reference," Chan said.

"It shows at a glance where the market stands and how it is moving."

The index, developed by HKEX in collaboration with Bloomberg, tracks more than 300 offshore Renminbi bonds listed in the city.

Chan said the new index could set in motion a virtuous cycle, with funds and exchange-traded funds tracking it offering global investors convenient exposure to a diversified basket of RMB bonds.

Broader participation would lift secondary market trading, lower transaction costs, sharpen price discovery and ultimately reduce funding costs for issuers, he said.

Chan said the launch comes as RMB internationalisation enters a new phase, citing the launch of offshore mainland government bond futures in August and the acceptance of mainland government bonds as eligible non-cash collateral from this month.

He pointed to growing participation from overseas governments, corporates and multilateral development banks choosing Hong Kong to raise RMB funding, citing recent issuers from Indonesia and Kazakhstan.

He said this adds a new dimension to RMB internationalisation, with the currency becoming a funding currency for global issuers as well as an asset for international investors.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Chinese output up 5.3pc on intelligent manufacturing
articles.excerpt: Value-added industrial output increased by 5.3 percent in the first 10 months on the mainland, according to official figures on…
articles.fullText:
Value-added industrial output increased by 5.3 percent in the first 10 months on the mainland, according to official figures on Monday.

High-end and intelligent manufacturing contributed to over 50 percent of output during the period, a National Bureau of Statistics spokesperson said.

For October alone, output grew 4.8 percent from a year earlier.

Robust demand for AI-related products and cars helped pull the Chinese economy out of a second-quarter slowdown.

With third-quarter GDP growth running at 4.5 percent year on year, analysts believe Beijing remains on target to reach 4.5 to five percent without the need for significant additional stimulus.

Trade data released last week showed that goods exports soared in October as the global AI infrastructure buildout continued to elevate sales of high-tech goods.

Total retail sales of goods and services, a gauge that measures goods consumption and catering revenue, increased by 2.5 percent year on year in the first 10 months of this year.

For October alone, retail sales edged up 0.4 percent after growing 1.1 percent the previous month.

Economists in a poll had expected a 0.8 percent increase.

Services retail sales grew 4.9 percent in the first 10 months, narrowing from five percent growth in the first three quarters.

There is huge potential for consumption but people's capacity and willingness to spend need to be enhanced, a bureau spokesperson said.

An AI-driven export boom has powered China's economic growth this year and looks set to shelter overall growth from external and domestic headwinds into 2027.

Fixed-asset investment dropped 8.1 percent in the first 10 months, compared to a 7.2 percent drop in the first nine months.

The surveyed urban unemployment rate in China fell to 5.1 percent in October from 5.2 percent in September.

New home prices declined again in October, albeit at the lowest annual rate in almost a year, extending a years-long slump that has eroded market confidence, sapped consumer spending and squeezed local government income.

Prices fell 0.1 percent versus September, when they also fell by the same percentage.

Beijing has in recent months introduced fresh support, including measures for steering cheaper credit into a range of sectors including infrastructure and technology, as well as expanding support for home buyers.

Regulators also in early November rolled out a handful of measures, from conducting swap operations to upgrading a lending facility for stock buybacks by listed companies, as part of efforts to stabilise struggling capital markets.

Looking ahead, policymakers will step up policy support for domestic demand if the tailwind from the AI boom tapers off, analysts said. (Xinhua/Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China confirms Xi to hold summit with Trump, Putin
articles.excerpt: The Foreign Ministry in Beijing on Monday said President Xi Jinping would hold a China-Russia-US summit with his Russian counterpart…
articles.fullText:
The Foreign Ministry in Beijing on Monday said President Xi Jinping would hold a China-Russia-US summit with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin and US leader Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday.

Speaking at a regular news briefing, ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the meeting would be of groundbreaking significance.

"This will be the first face-to-face meeting in history among the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States. They will exchange in-depth views on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance.

"In the current situation, the three countries bear an important responsibility to cooperate in addressing global challenges and to promote world peace and stability. Strengthening communication among China, Russia and the US, managing differences, and stabilising relations is in the interest of all three countries, meets the expectations of the international community, and helps stabilise the global situation and advance dialogue and cooperation."

Plans for the three-way summit were earlier confirmed by the White House on Friday and the Kremlin on Saturday.

The Trump administration has said that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss international issues of pressing concern.

Trump does plan on discussing the Iran war with Xi and Putin, but will steer away from bringing up the topic of Ukraine, according to a senior US official who briefed reporters on the condition of anonymity. (Xinhua/AP)

articles.title: HK stocks up amid regional jitters over US tech crunch
articles.excerpt: Asian shares fell on Monday after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief…
articles.fullText:
Asian shares fell on Monday after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive, with the chipmaker's earnings and Anthropic's initial public offering this week set to test whether the artificial intelligence-fuelled bull market still has further to run.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 71 points, or 0.3 percent, at 23,708.

The China enterprises index rose 27 points, or 0.35 percent, to 7,965 while the tech index climbed 15 points, or 0.41 percent, to 3,828.

The minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting are also due on Wednesday, while a parade of Fed speakers will also be on the bill this week.

Markets will be alert for any hint of policymakers being receptive to the idea of an outsized 50-basis-point interest rate hike next month.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 22 points, or 0.63 percent, at 3,611.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 86 points, or 0.79 percent, lower at 10,881 while the ChiNext Index fell 30 points, or 1.26 percent, to 2,395.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 205 points, or 0.34 percent, higher at 61,348 before going the other way to be 893 points lower at one stage before lunch amid jitters over Nvidia earnings.

In Seoul, the Kospi inched up 15 points, or 0.28 percent, at 5,305 before, like the Nikkei and for the same reasons, plunging to be 122 points lower at one stage before noon.

The losses on the tech-heavy Japanese and South Korean benchmarks came as Nvidia, the poster child of a four-year US bull market, has seen its market value tumble from about US$5.8 trillion in early October to US$3.9 trillion as of Friday, LSEG data showed, as investors rushed for the exit after Huang's departure.

Analysts expect earnings growth of 90 percent on revenue of US$109 billion in Nvidia's fiscal third quarter when its earnings are due on Tuesday, LSEG data showed, with all eyes on whether the chipmaker will stick to its bullish outlook for next year under new management.

"Options markets imply an earnings-day move of approximately +/-7 percent, yet I question whether the quarterly numbers will carry their usual significance," said Chris Weston, head of research at foreign exchange brokerage Pepperstone.

"Nvidia may well deliver another exceptional beat and raise at tomorrow's earnings, but investors are increasingly trying to value a business in FY2028 and FY2029 potentially without the individual who architected its competitive advantage."

The Financial Times reported Huang had discussed with confidants the possibility of returning as chief executive.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs to "go outside the company" for a new CEO.

Just two days after Nvidia's earnings, trading in Claude chatbot creator Anthropic is scheduled to begin, setting up a real-time barometer for sentiment on the AI trade.

The firm's IPO has drawn more institutional interest than SpaceX, insiders said. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: New World shares slump amid rights issue plan
articles.excerpt: Shares of New World Development tumbled more than 45 percent at the open of trade on Monday after the property…
articles.fullText:
Shares of New World Development tumbled more than 45 percent at the open of trade on Monday after the property developer proposed a HK$24.9 billion rights issue plan.

The plan offers shareholders 11 rights shares for every existing share at HK$0.90 each, representing an 81.5 percent discount to the last closing price of HK$4.87.

New World Development, the most indebted among its peers in the city, has been trying to cut debt, dispose of assets and bolster liquidity amid tight credit conditions and a weak property market.

Shares of New World slumped to HK$2.655 at open, an all-time low since its listing in 1980.

After the share fall on Monday, New World's market value shrank to less than HK$8 billion, three times less than the rights issue size.

"While investors had long been expecting a rights issue... (the) discount is likely to be beyond most investors’ prior expectations," investment bank JP Morgan said in a report.

It expected the rights issue would ease New World's near-term liquidity risk, but the proceeds alone were unlikely to completely eliminate its liquidity stress, with adjusted net gearing still above 70 percent.

Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises (CTFE), which owns about 45.3 percent of the company, has committed to taking up its full entitlement and fully underwrite any unsubsidised shares.

The maximum CTFE commitment is about HK$18.7 billion.

New World plans to use about 34 percent of the proceeds to prepay 10 percent of about HK$82 billion in bank loans and extend the maturity of the rest by two years.

It aims to cut total debt by between HK$40 billion and HK$50 billion by the end of 2031, to stand at between HK$93 billion and HK$103 billion.

A shareholder meeting on January 5 next year will seek approval for the rights issue plan, with a threshhold of than 50 percent set for independent shareholders.

Shares of New World resumed trading on Monday after suspension on Friday for the announcement. (Reuters)
